title: Monthly level changes in Superior and Michigan-Huron had higher correlation in 1972-2025 after seasonal means were removed
abstract: We tested whether a prior rise in annual-change correlation also occurred in monthly level changes. Coordinated v2025 levels gave 636 paired months in 1919-1971 and 648 in 1972-2025. We removed each calendar month's mean change within each period. Pearson correlation rose from 0.328 to 0.450. The late-minus-early change was +0.122, with a conditional 95% five-year block interval of +0.025 to +0.217. Three- and ten-year blocks and removal of 2013-2014 kept positive intervals. A shorter 1950-2025 comparison had an interval that included zero. All four calendar-quarter joint bands included zero. Thus, annual averaging alone is not needed for the full-record pattern, but a specific season and a general increase through time are not established. Levels cannot separate shared weather, lake flow, regulation and source changes. The package includes monthly inputs, source hashes, code, draws, a figure, a separate arithmetic audit and an offline repeat.

display.caption: Monthly change correlations after separate seasonal means are removed. Blue intervals show marginal 95% limits. Gray bars show joint 95% bands for the four calendar quarters. All intervals condition on the source snapshot and block assumptions.
